title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Header: 'gr. de Galois motiv. de F_p'. The page computes the motivic Galois group G of the category of (semisimple, Tate-conjecture) motives over F_p, together with its p-adic and archimedean structure.

(1) G is a pro-group of multiplicative type over Q, G = D(Γ). Its character group Γ ⊂ Q̄* is the group of Weil p-numbers of all weights, with its natural Gal(Q̄/Q)-action. The torsion of Γ is μ_∞, which gives an exact sequence 0 → G° → G → Ẑ → 0 with:
- G° = D(Γ/μ_∞), a pro-torus;
- component group D(μ_∞) = constant Ẑ, because the Galois twists on μ_∞ and on its dual cancel.
In modern terms this is Milne's Weil-number pro-group P (with P° the Langlands–Rapoport/Milne Weil-number torus).

(2) Weight and Tate structure. There is a weight cocharacter i: G_m → G and a Tate character ε: G → G_m, with εi(λ) = λ² (the Tate motive has weight 2). Dually there are maps i*: Γ → Z (the weight) and ε*: Z → Γ, with ε*(1) = p, |λ| = p^{i*(λ)/2} and i*ε* = 2.
- Γ° = Ker i* is the group of 'Weil units': algebraic numbers of absolute value 1 at every archimedean place and units at all finite places ≠ p.
- Γ/(μ·p^Z) ≅ Z/2 × Γ°/μ. The Z/2 is the weight mod 2, split by ±√p, as the next page confirms.
- U, a corresponding subgroup (kernel), decomposes as μ_2-type × U°.

(3) Frobenius. The tautological inclusion Γ ⊂ Q̄* defines a canonical Frobenius element F ∈ G(Q).

(4) p-adic side. Let G_{F_p}^{cris} be the Tannakian group of F-isocrystals over F_p. These are Q_p-spaces with a linear automorphism, so this group is the algebraic hull of Z over Q_p, with reductive quotient D(Q̄_p*). The crystalline realization gives an epimorphism α: (G_{F_p})_red = D(Q̄_p*) → G_{Q_p}, with matching maps on component groups (Ẑ = Ẑ) and on identity components. Dually, α*: Γ → Q̄_p* is the canonical inclusion. Composing with the normalized p-adic valuation Q̄_p* → Q gives the slopes. The square passes to the quotients by roots of unity.

(5) Endomorphism algebras. For a simple motive M over F_p:
- A_M = End(M) has center Z_M = Q(F_M);
- A_M ⊗ Q_p ≅ End of the p-adic (crystalline) realization, by Tate–Honda if M is an abelian variety;
- A_M splits at every finite ℓ ≠ p.
The page breaks off at 'the invariants of the simple components of…', i.e. the Tate-type computation of local invariants: v(π)/v(q)·[Z_v:Q_p] at p-adic places, 1/2 at real places, 0 elsewhere.

The next page goes on to H²(Q,T), local Tate–Nakayama terms and p = ∞ contributions in M/2M. That is, it computes the cohomology class measuring the non-neutrality of the category, i.e. the motivic Galois gerbe of F_p.

Purpose: an explicit description of the motivic Galois group and gerbe over a finite field, assuming the standard and Tate conjectures.
errors: The arrow D(Γ) ⟵ D(racines de 1) is written in the character direction. On groups the map is G = D(Γ) → D(μ_∞) = Ẑ, induced by μ_∞ ⊂ Γ.
α* is drawn as a two-headed arrow. It should be α*: Γ → Q̄_p*, which is injective because α is an epimorphism.

'A ⊗_Q Q_p ≅ End(T_p(M))' is imprecise in characteristic p. One should use the Dieudonné module or crystalline realization (End of the F-isocrystal), not a p-adic Tate module, which is too small for non-ordinary abelian varieties.

Writing G as a group over Q with a Q-valued Frobenius is fine for the (commutative) band. However, the category of motives over F_p is not neutral over Q (supersingular elliptic curves give quaternion endomorphism algebras ramified at p and ∞). So a fiber functor over Q does not exist. The next page's H²(Q,T) computation appears to address exactly this, but this page leaves it implicit.
The mention of Tate–Honda implies this sheet postdates 1966–68 (Tate 1966, Honda 1968), not 1965. This bears on the dating of the folder.

ideas.what: Motivic Galois group of F_p is of multiplicative type with character group the Weil p-numbers; extension of Ẑ by a pro-torus D(Γ/μ)
ideas.modern_name: Weil-number pro-torus P / motivic Galois group of Mot(F_q)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Langlands–Rapoport (1987), Milne ('Motives over finite fields', 1994); partly Saavedra Rivano (1972)

ideas.modern_name: weight homomorphism w and Tate character t of the Weil-number group

ideas.what: Canonical Frobenius element F ∈ G(Q) given by the tautological embedding Γ ⊂ Q̄*
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius element of the motivic Galois group

ideas.modern_name: p-adic morphism of gerbes / Dieudonné–Manin realization into the Weil-number group

ideas.what: For simple motive M over F_p: End(M) has center Q(F_M), splits at ℓ≠p, p-adic completion equals End of crystalline realization; local invariants to be computed

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly computes the motivic Galois group over F_p as the Weil-number group D(Γ), with identity component D(Γ/μ) and component group Ẑ. He includes the weight/Tate structure, the canonical Frobenius in G(Q), and the crystalline comparison D(Q̄_p*) → G_{Q_p}. These are the ingredients of the Langlands–Rapoport/Milne Weil-number torus and pseudomotivic gerbe, usually credited to 1987–1994 work.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Shows Grothendieck approaching the gerbe-theoretic (non-neutral) description of Mot(F_p), later done by Langlands–Rapoport and Milne. Mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains a clear, essentially correct description of the motivic Galois group over F_p via Weil numbers, with the crystalline comparison. The literature credits this to Langlands–Rapoport/Milne (and partly Saavedra). It is unpublished Grothendieck work, but its content is now standard, so it is not a mathematical surprise.
transcription_corrections: '(nbs quadratiques[?] de val. abs. des[?] sur [-toutes-] les places ≠ p)' should read roughly 'nombres algébriques de val. abs. 1 sur [toutes] les places ≠ p (unités de Weil)'.

'Rotations[?] motiviques[?] F-constantes sur F_p' is probably a description of F-isocrystals/F-cristaux over F_p (i.e. Q_p-spaces with an automorphism F), whose reductive group is D(Q̄_p*). The margin 'analogues algébriques de Z' refers to the algebraic hull of Z.
'G_{\overline{F}_p}' at the left of the middle diagram is more likely the Tannakian group of (iso)crystals over F_p, not a group over F̄_p.
The α* arrow should be one-directional Γ → Q̄_p*, labelled 'l'inclusion canonique'.
'(Γ, ainsi que[?] la clôt. algébrique…)' likely reads '(Q̄ une clôture algébrique de Q, Γ engendré par les … qui définit Γ)'. Uncertain.
In the neighbouring transcription, 'voisinage de 1' is almost certainly a misreading of 'racines de 1'.
